established_physical_theory: 1-D steady conservation links surface flux, basal flux and integrated volumetric heat production
constant-property half-space surface conductive flux scales as age^-1/2
finite-thickness plate/basal-resupply models can approach finite old-age behavior
earth_observations: observed seafloor heat flow differs from conductive age-model predictions, especially at young ages
continental heat flow and radiogenic production vary laterally and by crustal layer
Earth global means and province observations are not ARCANA 210 Ma input
implementation_choices: ShellSet exact-zero heat-flow sentinel and qArray routing
qLim clamps and age<=0 -> qLim1 branch
arcana_inference: current continental reference flux may constrain the continental branch only after its role is governed
existing ocean age is a model input, not an already specified flux law

half_space_cooling.behavior: q proportional to t^-1/2; diverges as t approaches 0+ and continues declining without an old-age plateau.
half_space_cooling.strength: simple conductive approximation for young oceanic lithosphere
half_space_cooling.limits: poorly represents old-age depth/heat-flow flattening; idealized ridge boundary; observed young seafloor flux can be hydrothermally depressed.

plate_cooling.equation_family: Solve conductive cooling in a finite-thickness plate with fixed or parameterized basal thermal condition; model-specific.
plate_cooling.behavior: finite old-age asymptote under fixed basal-temperature plate formulation.
plate_cooling.strength: captures old-age flattening better than simple half-space in classical comparisons.
plate_cooling.limits: inferred thickness/basal temperature trade off with heat-flow/depth datasets and material-property assumptions; not a universal unique model.

GDH1.shellset_match: Qualified MOD_Data.f90 positive-age expression is algebraically identical after unit conversion; source comment attributes it to preferred GDH1 and cites Stein & Stein (1992).
GDH1.at_55_ma: branches join continuously at approximately 68.8 mW m-2
GDH1.age_zero: positive-age law is singular; qualified ShellSet separately assigns qLim1 when age<=0. That branch is implementation policy, not GDH1.
GDH1.applicability: Earth empirical age/depth and heat-flow fit, not a universal synthetic-planet law.

young_ocean_hydrothermal.finding: Hydrothermal advection can depress measured conductive heat flow over young ridge flanks; ridge-axis/focused discharge may instead produce high local values. Age, permeability, crust, sediments, and fluid pathways control variation.
young_ocean_hydrothermal.quantitative_evidence: Stein & Stein (1994) estimated about 34% of their predicted global oceanic heat flux was hydrothermal and a sealing age 65±10 Ma; authors describe global hydrothermal estimate as an upper bound affected by measurement-site bias.
young_ocean_hydrothermal.interpretation: Global Earth inference with sampling uncertainty; not a local correction coefficient or ARCANA parameter.

alternative_reference_models.name: Grose/Afonso comprehensive plate models
alternative_reference_models.description: Include oceanic crust insulation, variable properties and hydrothermal circulation; young-age predictions differ substantially from GDH1.

alternative_reference_models.name: Korenaga & Korenaga 2021 reference model
alternative_reference_models.description: Variable-property conductive evolution with internal-heating and secular-cooling corrections; provides parameterized age-dependent reference results.

alternative_reference_models.name: Holdt et al. 2025 revised plates
alternative_reference_models.description: Reassesses analytical/numerical plate models against updated depth and temperature observations and discusses inversion tradeoffs.

continental_relation.equation: q_surface = q_base + integral_0^H A(z) dz; for A(z)=A0 exp(-z/D), radiogenic contribution=A0*D*(1-exp(-H/D)).
assumptions: specified source distribution, basal flux, geometry and boundary conditions
continental_relation.interpretation: Surface heat flow can be a valid prescribed Neumann boundary for a forward geotherm, but does not uniquely determine internal source layers or geotherm by itself.
findings: continental crustal production is stratified and laterally variable
global analyses find no positive crust-thickness/surface-heat-flow correlation
continental geotherms do not correlate simply with rock/thermotectonic age

earth_observational_context.meaning: estimated crustal radiogenic contribution to surface flux under stated crust/composition assumptions

age_zero_and_q_limits.literature_conclusion: No reviewed source establishes these exact q-limit controls as universal geophysical values.

arcana_state_reconciliation.continental_reference_surface_heat_flow_: Exists on cell support as continental domain reference; not complete global flux, not ocean flux, not 64,442-node FEG field; role as direct input versus target/reference must be governed.
